title: What are two, three and more parts of one eighth?
description: The paper strip is folded once more to make eight equal parts of one eighth each. Counting two, three, up to eight of those parts gives the lengths in the blank boxes. Keeko's doubt, that three times one eighth is three twenty fourths, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: when parts of the same unit are counted, the top number counts the parts and the bottom number stays the same. Watch for students who multiply the bottom number as well.

source: Do it once more! Fill in the blank boxes. 2 times 1/8 = ___, 4 times 1/8 = ___, 6 times 1/8 = ___, 8 times 1/8 = 8/8 = 1.
video_script.why: The child folds the strip into eight equal parts and counts parts of one eighth, seeing that the top number counts the parts while the bottom number stays eight.
video_script.substitution: Count parts of one eighth the way parts of one fourth were counted, and fill each box with the number of parts over eight.
video_script.anchor: A paper strip one unit long, folded into eight equal parts, with a row of boxes to fill for two, three, up to eight parts
video_script.wrong_answer: three times one eighth is three twenty fourths
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the eight by three as well and says three twenty fourths. Twenty four equal parts would be much smaller pieces, but the three parts are three of the eight parts on the strip, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Three parts of one eighth make three eighths

final_answer.spoken: two eighths, three eighths, four eighths, five eighths, six eighths, seven eighths, and eight eighths, which is one whole

video_script.fraction_reading: one eighth, two eighths, three eighths, and so on, up to eight eighths
never_show: 3/24 as the length of three parts
maths_rules: the strip is 1 unit long; it had 4 equal parts of 1/4
folding once more splits each part into 2: 4 x 2 = 8 equal parts, each 1/8 unit
several parts together: the number of parts goes on top and the 8 stays at the bottom: 2/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8
8 x 1/8 = 8/8 = 1, the whole strip (given in the book)
slip: multiplying the bottom number as well gives 3 x 8 = 24, so 3/24, a far shorter length than 3 of the 8 parts
video_script.design: One idea: count parts of one eighth; the bottom number stays eight. Assumes one half and one fourth from the last videos. Wrong idea: multiplying the bottom number as well. The strip stays on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the paper strip of one unit with four equal parts, and a row of empty boxes below it

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.strip: the strip appears with four equal parts
marks.fold: each of the four parts is folded in two, giving a strip of eight equal parts
marks.ask: the words fill in the boxes appear above a row of empty boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the paper strip again.
<bookmark mark='strip'/>The strip is one unit long and has four equal parts.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>We fold it once more, and it has eight equal parts.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How long are two parts, three parts, and all the way up to eight parts?

beats.on_screen: the strip holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the strip is drawn as a long bar of one unit with four equal parts, each part marked 1/4

marks.unit: the strip is drawn as a long bar and marked as the whole unit
marks.fourths: the bar is cut into four equal parts and each part is marked one fourth

beats.colours: the strip = amber, the parts = teal
narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>The strip is one whole unit long.
<bookmark mark='fourths'/>The last fold gave four equal parts, and each part is one fourth of a unit.

beats.on_screen: Given: a strip of 1 unit with 4 equal parts, each part folded once more

marks.given: the strip with four parts and the new fold are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a strip of one unit with four equal parts, and each part is folded once more.

beats.on_screen: To find: the length of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of the new parts

marks.find: the words length of two up to eight parts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the length of two parts, three parts, and so on up to eight parts.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: each of the 4 parts is folded in two: 4 x 2 = 8 equal parts, each part is 1/8 unit

marks.fold: each of the four parts is folded into two equal parts
marks.eight: the opened strip shows eight equal parts and one part is marked 1/8

narration: <bookmark mark='fold'/>Step one, fold each of the four parts in two. Four times two gives eight equal parts.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>One unit is shared into eight equal parts, so each part is one eighth of a unit.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: count parts from the left end; the number of parts goes on top and the 8 stays at the bottom

marks.count: parts are counted from the left end, and the count is written on top of a line
marks.stay: the number 8 stays at the bottom because every part is still one eighth

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count the parts from the left end, the same way as the example in your book. The number of parts goes on top.
<bookmark mark='stay'/>The bottom number stays eight, because each part is still one eighth.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check, 8 parts reach the right end: 8 x 1/8 = 8/8 = 1, the whole strip

marks.end: the eighth part reaches the right end of the strip
marks.whole: the line 8 x 1/8 = 8/8 = 1 is written under the strip

narration: <bookmark mark='end'/>Step three, check. Eight parts reach the right end of the strip.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Eight times one eighth is eight eighths, and that is one whole unit.

marks.list: the boxes fill with two eighths up to seven eighths, then eight eighths = 1

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Three parts of one eighth make three eighths.
<bookmark mark='list'/>In the same way, two parts make two eighths, and four parts make four eighths. Five, six and seven parts make five, six and seven eighths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; a strip cut into twenty four tiny parts is drawn under the strip of eight parts and three tiny parts are far shorter than three of the eight; the bubble is struck through

marks.fix: three tiny parts of a strip cut into twenty four are far shorter than three of the eight parts, and the bubble is struck through
marks.stay: the bottom number eight is circled and stays the same

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three times one eighth is three twenty fourths.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But twenty four equal parts would be much smaller pieces. Our three parts are three of the eight parts on the strip.
<bookmark mark='stay'/>The bottom number tells the size of each part. It stays eight when we count more parts.
